title: Yoneda coefficient splice versus the signed localization boundary
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:W=T-Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $0\to G_1\to G_2\to G_3\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $h\in G_3(W)$. Work in their ordinary derived category and Ext groups [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-pc-ext]. Put $F=i_*\mathbf Z_Z$ and let $e_h\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_T(F,G_3)$ be the pushout of
$$0\to j_!\mathbf Z_W\to\mathbf Z_T\to F\to0$$
[lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] along the map $j_!\mathbf Z_W\to G_3$ adjoint to $1\mapsto h$. Let $k\in\operatorname{Ext}^1_T(G_3,G_1)$ be the extension class of the coefficient sequence, and let $\delta_W:G_3(W)\to H^1(W,G_1)$ be its ordinary connecting map. For a nonnegative injective resolution $G_1\to J$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], let $H^q_Z(T,G_1)$ be derived kernel-of-restriction cohomology [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. Use the supported-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] and the signed relative realization [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology, lem-pur-divisor-torsor-boundary-signs]
$$C^q=J^q(T)\oplus J^{q-1}(W),\qquad D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}(a)-db),\qquad \partial[b]=[(0,-b)].$$
Normalize this identification on the kernel complex by sending a cocycle $z:F\to J^q$ to $(z\circ p,0)$, where $p:\mathbf Z_T\to F$. Then the Yoneda splice, in the order $k[1]\circ e_h:F\to G_1[2]$, corresponds to
$$\partial\bigl(\delta_W(h)\bigr)\in H^2_Z(T,G_1).$$
This is a positive equality. It concerns the Yoneda splice, with its derived shift, rather than the termwise connecting map of the short exact sequence of signed relative complexes. It holds for arbitrary $G_a$, including nontorsion $G_2,G_3$.

source.place: Tag 06XP, section-ext (Ext and composition); Tag 06XU, lemma-yoneda-extension, with definition-yoneda-extension and the Yoneda composition paragraph immediately after lemma-ext-1. Agent-stated signed localization refinement of these constructions and the open-closed sequence; the exact comparison is not a verbatim Stacks assertion.

proof.text: Keep the given resolution $G_1\to J$ fixed. Abelian etale sheaves have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $G_3\xrightarrow{\epsilon}K$ using [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero], and apply [lem-sp-horseshoe-prescribed-resolutions] to the coefficient sequence with these two prescribed endpoint resolutions. Write its middle resolution as $I^q=J^q\oplus K^q$ and its differential as $d_I^q(a,c)=(d_Ja+t^qc,d_Kc)$. Thus $d_Jt^q+t^{q+1}d_K=0$. Write the middle augmentation as $G_2\to I^0$, $y\mapsto(l(y),\epsilon g(y))$, where $g:G_2\to G_3$. The augmentation identities give $l|_{G_1}=\epsilon_1$ and $d_Jl=-t^0\epsilon g$.

source.place: Tags 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses), prescribed endpoint resolutions and block differential

proof.text: Put $A=j_!\mathbf Z_W$, $B=\mathbf Z_T$ and write the open-closed sequence as $0\to A\xrightarrow{a}B\xrightarrow{p}F\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact]. A map $\mathbf Z_T\to M$ is determined by the image of $1$, and a section defines the map by integer multiplication and restriction. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], $\operatorname{Hom}(A,M)=M(W)$, with precomposition by $a$ equal to restriction. Injectivity of $K^0$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends $\epsilon h:A\to K^0$ to a map $u:B\to K^0$. Since $d_K\epsilon h=0$, there is a unique $z:F\to K^1$ with $zp=d_Ku$. Moreover $d_Kz=0$, since this is zero after the epimorphism $p$.

Let $E_h$ be the middle sheaf of the pushout defining $e_h$. The maps $\epsilon:G_3\to K^0$ and $u:B\to K^0$ agree on $A$, hence induce $v:E_h\to K^0$. Its differential factors as $z$ on the quotient $F$, so there is a morphism of short exact sequences from $0\to G_3\to E_h\to F\to0$ to $0\to G_3\to K^0\to Z^1(K)\to0$, with quotient map $\bar z:F\to Z^1(K)$. The latter row is exact because $K$ resolves $G_3$. Naturality [lem-sc-p1-ext-class-naturality] identifies $e_h$ with the pullback of its class by $\bar z$. By [lem-amb-first-resolution-extension-class] that class is the negative of the cycles-inclusion cocycle. Thus, using [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution], $e_h$ is represented by $-z:F\to K^1$. This minus sign is essential.

source.place: Tags 06XR (lemma-compute-ext-resolutions), 06XV (lemma-ext-1); explicit first-resolution sign from lem-amb-first-resolution-extension-class

proof.text: The identity $d_Jl=-t^0\epsilon g$ from step 1 yields a morphism from the coefficient sequence to $0\to G_1\to J^0\to Z^1(J)\to0$, with quotient map $c:G_3\to Z^1(J)$ whose cycles inclusion is $-t^0\epsilon$. It is a cycles map since $d_Jt^0\epsilon=-t^1d_K\epsilon=0$. Naturality [lem-sc-p1-ext-class-naturality] and the first-row sign [lem-amb-first-resolution-extension-class] therefore give $k=-[c]=[t^0\epsilon]$. The maps $t^q$ form a chain map $t:K\to J[1]$, by $d_Jt+t d_K=0$ and the negative differential on $J[1]$. The resolution description [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] then says that this chain map represents $k$ after inverting $G_3\to K$ and $G_1[1]\to J[1]$. In particular its component in degree one is $t^1$, without an extra negation of a shifted chain map.

source.place: Tags 06XR and 06XV; first-row sign, and the cochain shift convention

proof.text: By [lem-sc-ext-yoneda-composition-derived], the product in the question is obtained by shifting the representative of $k$ by one and composing with the representative of $e_h$. Steps 3 and 4 consequently give the cocycle $w=-t^1z:F\to J^2$ for $k[1]\circ e_h$. The cocycle-to-derived-morphism formula of [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] justifies canceling the intermediate resolution isomorphism: explicitly the two roofs compose to $F\xrightarrow{-z}K[1]\xrightarrow{t[1]}J[2]\xleftarrow{\epsilon_1[2]}G_1[2]$.

source.place: Tag 06XP (section-ext), composition paragraph following lemma-ext-1, and Tag 06XR

proof.text: Put $x=t^0u\in J^1(T)$ and $b=x|_W=t^0\epsilon h\in J^1(W)$. In the split horseshoe of step 1 the section $r=(0,\epsilon h)\in I^0(W)$ lifts $h$, and $d_Ir=(b,0)$. The coefficient-boundary formula in [lem-pur-divisor-torsor-boundary-signs] therefore gives $\delta_W(h)=[b]$. This application uses its clause for arbitrary short exact sequences of abelian sheaves; no torsion condition is imposed. Directly, $d_Jb=-t^1d_K\epsilon h=0$.

source.place: Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1); ordinary lift-and-differentiate representative in the statement of lem-pur-divisor-torsor-boundary-signs

proof.text: The block differential identity now gives $d_Jx=-t^1d_Ku=-t^1zp=wp$. Thus $wp$ vanishes on $W$. Indeed $b$ is a cocycle and restriction commutes with $d_J$. Under [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] with $A=\mathbf Z$, and the stipulated kernel normalization, the cocycle $w$ represents $(wp,0)=(d_Jx,0)$ in the signed relative complex [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology]. This is also the kernel-of-restriction model of [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]: $\operatorname{Hom}(F,J^q)$ is the kernel of $J^q(T)\to J^q(W)$ by the exact sequence and adjunction of step 2. Surjectivity of this restriction follows from the same injective lifting property used there. Consequently its inclusion into the signed fibre is a quasi-isomorphism: the quotient is the contractible complex on $J(W)$, with differential $(a,b)\mapsto(da,a-db)$ and contraction $(a,b)\mapsto(b,0)$.

source.place: Tag 06XR and the kernel normalization; explicit signed-fibre quotient contraction

proof.text: Finally, in the prescribed signed coordinates $D(x,0)=(d_Jx,b)$. Hence $(d_Jx,0)-(0,-b)=D(x,0)$, so the two degree-two cocycles have the same class. The boundary convention of [lem-pur-divisor-torsor-boundary-signs] sends $[b]$ to $[(0,-b)]$. Together with steps 5–7 this is exactly $k[1]\circ e_h=\partial(\delta_W(h))$ under the normalized supported-Hom identification. The calculation used the given arbitrary resolution $J$ and arbitrary abelian coefficient sheaves, so it proves the assertion for every resolution allowed in the statement, including nontorsion $G_2,G_3$.
